section_summary: The section concludes one set of regulations enforcing the Opium Ordinance of Formosa, including licensing fees, penalties, and supplementary provisions effective in 1929. It then prints another set of enforcement regulations governing prepared and medicinal opium, with rules for smokers, sellers, recordkeeping, storage, export, and scientific or medical use. The final page is a 1942 State Department transmittal note concerning the Bechuanaland Protectorate’s annual report on opium and other dangerous drugs for 1941.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Enforcement of the Opium Ordinance of Formosa: Concluding Articles and Supplementary Regulations
subfiles.about: Concluding provisions establish administrative procedures, fees, penalties, and transitional arrangements under the Opium Ordinance of Formosa.
subfiles.summary: Formosa Opium Ordinance's concluding articles cover residence changes, permit reissuance, enforcement fees, dealer discipline, and gubernatorial powers; penalties include imprisonment, fines, or detention; supplementary provisions preserve prior appointments, effective January 9, 1929.

subfiles.title: Regulations for the Enforcement of the Opium Ordinance of Formosa: Articles 1–28
subfiles.about: Regulations control the possession, consumption, sale, storage, export, and medical or scientific use of prepared and medicinal opium in Formosa.
subfiles.summary: The regulations limit the quantities possessed by authorized opium smokers and require permits, purchase books, and approved disposal of opium dross. Wholesale agents and retailers must be licensed, sell at official prices, maintain transaction records, submit monthly reports, and comply with storage directions. Further articles regulate medicinal-opium wholesalers, exports, transfers among medical professionals and drug trades, scientific-use permits, repurchase or destruction of stocks, and official oversight of storage. The publication was printed by the Taiheiyosha Press in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the Bechuanaland Protectorate Annual Narcotics Report for 1941
subfiles.to: Administrator of the Federal Security Agency
subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits a League of Nations document containing the Bechuanaland Protectorate’s annual report on opium and other dangerous drugs for 1941.
subfiles.summary: Note encloses Bechuanaland's 1941 annual narcotics report, submitted under the 1931 Limitation Convention via the League of Nations, for Public Health Service records.
